item.title: Ultrabroadband Omnidirectional Super-Black Hierarchical Metamaterials
item.description:
CCS Chemistry, Ahead of Print.
DOI:10.31635/ccschem.026.202608341
Super-black materials are indispensable for advanced optics, precision instrumentation, energy technologies, and functional applications. However, achieving near-perfect absorption simultaneously across the ultraviolet to mid-infrared (MIR) spectrum and at incidence angles up to 80° remains a long-standing challenge. Herein, we propose a hierarchical light-trapping metamaterial with a microscopically disordered yet macroscopically ordered architecture, where radially divergent dandelion-like hierarchical carbon spheres (DHCs) are functionally coupled with an ordered, periodically arranged micro-cone array. The DHCs act as isotropic light-randomization units, suppressing specular reflection and enhancing angular insensitivity. Meanwhile, the micro-cone array guides light via multiple internal reflections, prolonging the optical path and promoting photon capture. This cross-scale synergy establishes a three-dimensional gradient refractive index, enabling the metamaterial to achieve average absorptances of 99.69% in the solar spectrum (0.25–2.5 μm) and 99.01% in the mid-infrared regime (2.5–16 μm). Notably, the metamaterial maintains over 98% absorption even at an 80° incident angle, which exemplifies its exceptional ultrabroadband and omnidirectional absorption performance. Our work demonstrates a hierarchical divide-and-conquer strategy and provides a new paradigm for developing high-performance optical metamaterials for complex light-field environments.
